# Query-Driven Visualization
Also called: QDV
## Overview
Query-Driven Visualization (QDV) integrates database technologies with visualization strategies to address the increasing size and complexity of scientific datasets [S1, unofficial]. It uses user-specified selection queries to identify spatial regions of interest, reducing the data subset for efficient analysis and visualization [S1, unofficial]. Unlike siblings that focus on hardware [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) or spatial partitioning for rendering performance, QDV focuses on semantic data reduction, allowing users to extract meaningful subsets (e.g., combustion fronts, pollution areas) based on domain-specific criteria before rendering [S1, unofficial].

## Background
Query-Driven Visualization was first presented by Stockinger et al., who demonstrated the coupling of visualization with high-performance query technology [S1, unofficial]. The technique was developed to handle the continually increasing size and complexity of scientific datasets [S1, unofficial]. It is used in the DEX software system by Stockinger et al. [S1, unofficial]. In this context, QDV is applied to extract function field features, such as golf courses, water, and pollution areas, from hyperspectral and air quality simulation data [S1, unofficial]. Features are defined as spatial regions where 1-dimensional functions are similar, specified as Boolean [range queries](#13751-feature-query.md) over closed intervals [S1, unofficial].
